move: card stack peels upward one by one, digit rolls, fresh stack returns
how: Five portrait image cards share a slot with depth(k) poses of y -40k / scale 1-0.06k and a black dim overlay at 0.22k opacity. A headline rises from y 60, a footer fades, a thin bar fills scaleX 0→1 linearly over the whole duration and every inner image drifts xPercent -3→3 with scale to 1.06. Every 0.72s from 0.35s the front card peels to y -1800 with rotation -7 (power3.in 0.55s), the remaining cards re-pose one step forward with expo.out and their dims lighten, and a counter digit rolls out yPercent -100 with opacity, is replaced via set(textContent), and rolls in from +100 (move). At 84% the fifth card peels off, the digit resets to 1, and the first four cards return from y 1700 / rotation 5 with move at 0.05s offsets, dims restored by set, so the stack is fresh for the loop.
adapt: Replace the five images and captions, the headline and footer, and the card count (STEP is 0.72s for five in 4s); keep depth()'s 40px / 6% pitch and the 0.55s power3.in peel.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the stack of N cards with dims and the counter, applying the depth() sets; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with T0 = 0.09D, STEP = 0.18D and the return at 0.86D. The digit set(textContent) and card selectors must be el-scoped; the fromTo returns already carry immediateRender:false.
caveats: digit text is swapped with set(textContent) and can go stale when scrubbing backwards
